title: I REALIZE BTW that (a) none of these are as scary as most of what we ...
transcript: here are the top 10 spookiest theater productions I've ever seen from least scary to most scary so I'm not talking about Beetlejuice or Little Shop of horrors I'm talking about the shows that actually give you that shot of frightened adrenaline and send chills down your spine. in 10th place I have the Weir by Connor Mcpherson which is less scary because it's about people telling ghost stories but in the play they supposedly really happened and when we get deep into the stories they can get very eerie in ninth place I have the stage version of the vampire movie Let the Right One In which I would say leans more wistful and unsettling but there's at least one unforgettable jump scare. next I have The Thin Place by Lucas Hnath which is about a woman who goes to a medium to get in touch with her dead mother and similarly there's a sequence toward the end where she goes into her abandoned childhood home and it really got my heart racing. next I have Stranger Things the First Shadow which is scary in a different way it's less spooky and more just gruesome and intense but it can be quite frightening in that way. in sixth place I have Grey House which I know a lot of people were disappointed by it wasn't as scary as the marketing made it seem I'm actually a huge defender of this play but I do agree in the sense that it's not as scary because you're more or less rooting for the characters making the scary things happen nevertheless there are some really freaky and disturbing parts. In 5th place I have 2:22 a Ghost Story where not as many scary things *happen* but the eerie premise very much looms over the whole thing and similar to a lot of the shows I've already mentioned I'd say there was one sequence that really got me on the edge of my seat. in 4th place I have a Ghost in your Ear where the story within the story, I would say, took a while to really get under my skin but eventually I was feeling the frights especially when the lines between fiction and reality in the play begin to blur. in 3rd place I have kinda the original it predates everything else on this list The Woman in black for a long time this was really the gold standard of like genuinely frightening horror theater and not just the iconography of horror but I do think the framing device undercut it a little bit sometimes it got a little too silly. in second place I have Paranormal Activity which, between the story and the stage effects does a great job providing a lot of different scares and just kind of keeping you in a sustained way in that frightened state for so much of the show. but in 1st place, maybe a surprise sleeper contender I have, from the same director as Paranormal Activity, Viola’s Room. this was an immersive promenade theater experience where you're wearing headphones and it has kind of a multi-layered dark fairy tale energy which starts out more alluring and exciting but by the end I think it's really eerie I remember this scene toward the end where you're standing still in the dark around this really creepy tree and they're talking about the cloven footprints in the dirt around you and I think that might have been the most frightened I've ever felt in a theatrical experience
